title: Snowflake Fair Isle mittens
subtitle: Full mittens with a repeating snowflake motif in two-colour Fair Isle.
excerpt: Full mittens with a 6-round repeating snowflake motif in two-colour Fair Isle, worked in DK wool in the round. The snowflake sits on a plain stocking stitch field. Afterthought thumb. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: Simple 6-stitch snowflake motifs in two-colour knitting appear in Scandinavian folk-knitting books from the early 20th century. The specific chart here is a basic 6-round, 6-stitch snowflake derived from publicly documented Nordic folk-knitting patterns.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts x 28 rounds = 10 x 10 cm in stranded colourwork on 3.75 mm needles.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 18 (20, 22) cm with 1 to 2 cm negative ease.

glossaryTerms.definition: A style of stranded colourwork using two colours per round. The unused colour floats across the back. Floats longer than 5 stitches should be caught to prevent snagging.

A thumb opening made by working the thumb stitches in waste yarn during the hand, then returning after the hand is complete. The waste yarn is removed to reveal live stitches which are picked up and worked as the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: Full mittens with a repeating snowflake in two-colour
Fair Isle
, worked in DK wool in the round, with an
afterthought thumb
. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.

The snowflake chart repeats over 6 stitches and 6 rounds. Two repeats are worked on the body: one on the cuff just above the rib, and one on the hand near the wrist. The rest of the hand is plain MC stocking stitch. The construction uses
magic loop
on a long circular. Budget about 90 g of MC (200 m / 220 yards) and 15 g of CC (33 m / 36 yards), both DK weight.
What you need

items.name: MC (main colour)
items.qty: 90 g (about 200 m / 220 yards) of DK-weight wool, dark

items.name: CC (contrast colour)
items.qty: 15 g (about 33 m / 36 yards) of the same yarn, white or light

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 3: 1 for beginning of round, 1 for thumb, 1 for top shaping midpoint

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 30 cm of smooth contrasting yarn for the afterthought thumb

content.text: Gauge
22 stitches and 28 rounds to 10 cm in stranded colourwork on 3.75 mm needles. Swatch the snowflake chart before casting on.
Snowflake chart

attrs.heading: 6-stitch x 6-round snowflake repeat. All rounds RS. Read right to left.

items.name: Round 2
items.qty: *k2 CC, k1 MC, k1 CC, k2 MC*; repeat.

items.name: Round 3
items.qty: *k1 MC, k1 CC, k3 MC, k1 CC*; repeat.

content.text: Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Cast on and rib cuff
Using MC and the long-tail cast-on, cast on 42 (48, 48) stitches, a multiple of 6. Join to work in the round. Work 16 (18, 18) rounds of 2x2 rib in MC.
First snowflake band
Join CC. Work the 6-round snowflake chart once. Work 4 rounds in MC stocking stitch. Drop CC.
Hand body
Work 8 (10, 10) rounds in MC stocking stitch. Place the afterthought thumb: work the first 10 (12, 12) stitches with waste yarn, slip back, and work in MC to end. Continue for 6 more rounds.
Second snowflake band
Join CC again. Work the 6-round snowflake chart once. Work 4 rounds in MC stocking stitch. Drop CC.
Hand above second band
Continue in MC stocking stitch for 8 (10, 10) rounds.
Top shaping

Place a marker at the midpoint. Decrease round: k1, ssk, knit to 3 before midpoint, k2tog, k1, SM, k1, ssk, knit to last 3, k2tog, k1. Plain round. Repeat until 8 stitches remain. Draw yarn through and close.
Thumb
Remove waste yarn and pick up 10 (12, 12) stitches above and 10 (12, 12) below. Work 14 (16, 16) rounds in MC stocking stitch. Bind off.
Common faults
Snowflake centre stitch is off-centre: the chart start position shifted between rounds. Check the beginning-of-round marker before each chart round.
Floats too long on the all-MC plain rounds: CC is being carried across rather than cut and rejoined. For a 4-round gap between snowflake bands, cut CC and rejoin rather than carrying it.
Finishing
Weave in all tails on the wrong side. Block the mittens to open the snowflake pattern.
Care
Hand wash in cool water with wool-safe detergent. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next
